sources.content:
Complaint: Customer reported recurring broadband disconnections during evening hours around 8 PM; router already restarted twice.
Resolution: Recorded the evening drop pattern, confirmed the ONT status light changed during drops, skipped a repeat restart and requested a line test with the time pattern attached.
Previous troubleshooting: Router restarted twice

sources.title: KB-031: Evening broadband drops: time-pattern diagnostic
sources.excerpt: Symptoms: Broadband drops repeatedly at a similar time of day, often in the evening, even after the router has been restarted. Resolution steps: 1. Record the exact times the drops occur over several days. 2. Check whether the router/ONT status lights change…
sources.content:
Symptoms: Broadband drops repeatedly at a similar time of day, often in the evening, even after the router has been restarted.
Resolution steps:
1. Record the exact times the drops occur over several days.
2. Check whether the router/ONT status lights change when the connection drops.
3. Test whether a wired device drops at the same time as Wi-Fi devices.
4. If the customer has already restarted the router, do not repeat the restart; move to the line test request.
5. Request a line test through the approved support process and attach the recorded time pattern.
Escalate when: Drops continue at a repeating time after the router restart, or the customer relies on the service for work.
Caution: Do not promise compensation or a fix date.
Source note: SYNTHETIC / DEMO DATA - not real telecom operator data.

sources.title: KB-010: Broadband disconnects intermittently
sources.excerpt: Symptoms: Fixed broadband connection drops and reconnects intermittently. Resolution steps: 1. Check router/ONT status indicators. 2. Restart the equipment. 3. Observe whether the connection drops again. 4. Record the time pattern of the drops for escalation…
sources.content:
Symptoms: Fixed broadband connection drops and reconnects intermittently.
Resolution steps:
1. Check router/ONT status indicators.
2. Restart the equipment.
3. Observe whether the connection drops again.
4. Record the time pattern of the drops for escalation if intermittent drops continue.
Escalate when: Intermittent drops continue after the equipment restart.
Caution: Do not attribute drops to the customer's equipment without status evidence.
Source note: SYNTHETIC / DEMO DATA - not real telecom operator data.
